name: react-native-spritestudio
description: SpriteStudio animation player for React Native (New Architecture / Nitro + Skia)
//peerDependencies: One line per package: the oldest line the Nitro/Skia side was compiled
against, so a wider range would claim a version nobody has built. The
workspace `overrides` pin the line example/ builds and runs against, which
is the same or newer; `expo install` gives users Expo's own, which is also
inside the range. Move the overrides by hand, not when the registry does;
that is why Dependabot is told to leave these five alone.
The caret does the right thing on both shapes: ^0.88.0-rc.1 is the 0.88
line, its release candidates included (a caret locks the minor below 1.0.0),
`expo` is the exception: optional, and only the config plugin loads it.
//devDependencies: `react-test-renderer` is pinned to the exact `react` the workspace `overrides`
chose, not a caret: React refuses to run against a renderer from a
different build, so the two move together. It is deprecated in React 19 and
is still the only renderer that does not need a DOM, which is what the
`view/` tests need -- @testing-library/react-native sits on it for the same
reason. Move it when react moves.
//publishConfig: npm tags whatever is published as `latest` regardless of the prerelease identifier, so a 7.0.0-beta.1 with no tag here would be what a bare `npm i react-native-spritestudio` installs. `beta` matches the identifier in the version and what SSPlayerForWgpu publishes under.
//browser: Not web support — the stub barrel, so an app that ships web as well as native can still build its web bundle (built from src/index.web.ts).
